items.title: Policy Circle: subsidy alone won't close India's container cost gap with China
items.text: A 30 Oct analysis of the CMPS cites Business Standard industry estimates of about $1,700 per TEU for Chinese boxes against $2,200-2,400 in India, a gap of roughly $500-700 (about 29-41% by the outlet's own calculation). It notes the 70% domestic-content requirement through 2031-32, rising to 90% from 2032-33, could lift costs if Indian inputs stay dearer than imports. It also says subsidies 'cannot substitute indefinitely for lower production costs'. For listed names the point is that the scheme's value depends on guidelines and on makers competing once support tapers. The article repeats the Maersk 1,000-box order for DCM Shriram, which the company denied on 6 Jul 2026, so that claim is not treated as confirmed here.

items.title: Kalyani Cast-Tech hits 5% upper circuit, Jupiter Wagons up 8% after container scheme approval
items.text: In early trade on 29 Oct, a day after the Cabinet cleared the Rs 10,000 cr Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme, Kalyani Cast-Tech hit its 5% upper circuit at Rs 1,210.50 on BSE and Jupiter Wagons rose 8.24% to Rs 195.97 on NSE. Upstox's coverage quotes no analysts and describes Kalyani's business as directly aligned with the scheme. The same report puts the listed-company link at stake for names such as DCM Shriram Industries (+4.75% to Rs 57.32), which it says depends on ownership structure and whether the relevant unit qualifies. That is a different company from DCM Shriram Ltd (DCMSHRIRAM). The move shows the market is pricing in a narrow theme before scheme guidelines or any sanctioned plant.

items.title: Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 cr Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to FY2039-40
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved the CMPS on 28 Oct 2026 with a Rs 10,000 crore outlay up to FY 2039-40: Rs 8,891 crore operational-expenditure assistance, Rs 859 crore for 3% interest subvention on term loans, and Rs 150 crore for testing and certification. Upstox reports thresholds of at least 1 lakh TEU for greenfield and 25,000 TEU for brownfield expansion, commissioned within three years of in-principle approval. The target is 7.5 lakh TEU annual capacity against roughly 2 million empty containers imported a year; the tenure is reported as 13 years by Upstox and 12 years by ETV Bharat, and eligibility criteria and guidelines are still to be notified.
